final.memo:
The Company is a classic example of a business where the intrinsic value of its timber assets is being cannibalized by a management team obsessed with empire-building through ill-timed capacity expansion. Management is currently sinking $66 million into a new Las Vegas towel plant despite a clear industry downturn and widespread oversupply, a move that sacrifices current cash generation for theoretical long-term gains [D01, D06]. Our initial thesis regarding asset stewardship is broken; while we have seen marginal operational improvements—including a recent labor contract—they are insufficient to justify the current stewardship of capital [D03, D07].

The governance structure is designed to insulate the board from accountability, utilizing an 80% approval hurdle for voting changes and a staggered board [D03, D07]. With the company delivering a staggering -33.1% ROE compared to a -4.1% peer average, the case for change is undeniable [D01, D06]. We have already engaged privately and registered our objection publicly, yet the management remains entrenched [D07].

We are moving to ESCALATE. We intend to force the issue of portfolio simplification and demand an immediate strategic review to separate the high-value timber assets from the manufacturing business [D01]. We will not wait for the next annual cycle to be ignored; we must hold the board accountable for the destruction of shareholder equity [D07].
